input.raw_text: Beneath the choppy tape the story is rotation, and it is not subtle. Money is leaving anything with a high beta: the FANG complex keeps getting sold into every bounce, semiconductors can't hold a bid, and the momentum unwind from October has simply continued under a different name. Meanwhile low-volatility ETFs are taking in assets at a pace I haven't seen since February, utilities have quietly outperformed the S&P by several points this month, and the dividend aristocrats are acting like a safe haven. Clients say they are not de-risking, they are re-pricing duration into an index that is pricing in December hikes and a trade war with no exit. Whether this is defensive positioning or the start of something worse, the tape doesn't say. It just says: own the bond proxies, sell the winners.
input.summary: Choppy U.S. equity trading reflects a pronounced rotation away from high-beta technology and momentum shares toward low-volatility, utility, dividend-growth, and other bond-proxy exposures. FANG and semiconductor rebounds are fading, while low-volatility funds are attracting unusually strong inflows and utilities are outperforming the S&P 500 this month. Client commentary frames the shift as duration repricing around expected December rate hikes and unresolved trade-war risk, but it remains unclear whether the move is limited defensive positioning or signals broader deterioration.

observations.statement: High-beta technology and momentum shares are weakening as rebounds fade
The momentum unwind underway since October is continuing
Low-volatility funds are attracting their strongest reported asset inflows since February
Utilities have outperformed the S&P 500 by several points this month
Dividend aristocrats are behaving as a perceived safe haven
Client commentary attributes the rotation to duration repricing around expected December rate hikes and unresolved trade-war risk
The available market behavior does not distinguish ordinary defensive positioning from broader deterioration
